=== REPORT: "The free energy principle for action and perception" (Buckley et al.) ===

## 1. The question, frozen

The paper answers several. The one its title and abstract make central is the FEP's explanatory claim, so that is what I test: **why do viable organisms perceive and act as they do — and how does the brain do it?** Range: biology from milliseconds of neuronal activity to evolutionary time. The paper narrows that range to one implementation (predictive coding, Gaussian R-density). Asked as a forward question ("what produces it"), with a side of "why can it not go otherwise". Held still throughout.

## 2. The explanation in parts

In the owners' words: the **recognition density** q(ϑ;µ); the **generative density** p(ϑ,ϕ)=p(ϕ|ϑ)p(ϑ); **informational free energy** F=∫q ln(q/p); **surprisal** −ln p(ϕ); the **Gaussian/Laplace approximation**; the **Laplace-encoded energy** E(µ,ϕ); the **generative equations** ϕ=g(µ;θ)+z, µ=μ̄+w; **generalised coordinates**; **perception** as gradient descent on µ; **action** as gradient descent on ϕ; **hierarchical learning** of θ and hyper-parameters; the claim that organisms are **“mandated, by the very fact of their existence”** to minimise dispersion; the **average-energy/entropy** analogy.

## 3. Part by part

| Part | Mark | From | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| R-density q(ϑ;µ) | **Held** | built | Remove it: there is no quantity to minimise. It is what the divergence is taken over. |
| G-density p(ϕ\|ϑ)p(ϑ) | **Held** | built, content asserted | Remove the likelihood: sensory data constrains nothing. Remove the prior: action has nothing to satisfy. *Which* g and f are true is asserted. |
| IFE F=∫q ln(q/p) | **Held** | built | The one object that both bounds surprisal (Jensen) and can be evaluated from q and p. Remove it and both jobs fail. |
| Surprisal −ln p(ϕ) | **Held if** | asserted | Held only by the job "the agent's model is well adapted". That job is asserted, not tested. |
| Gaussian R-density / Laplace | **Loose** | fitted | Swap in any sharply peaked, smooth density and the Taylor argument gives the same quadratic form. What is held is *peaked and smooth*, not *Gaussian*. Rename the part. |
| Laplace-encoded energy | **Held** | fitted | Remove the precision weights and the two errors cannot trade off. The exact quadratic form is inherited from the variational-Bayes lineage. |
| Generative equations | **Fixed** | owner, untested | g, f, additive noise and noise-independence are set by the modeller. |
| Generalised coordinates | **Held** | built | Drop them and a changing environment cannot be covered. Local linearity and independent noise are **Fixed**. |
| Perception (down on µ) | **Two routes** | built | Either this or action lowers F. |
| Action (down on ϕ) | **Two routes** | built | Same job as perception. |
| Hierarchical learning | **Held if** | asserted | Held only by the job "the environment is non-stationary in a way a fixed prior cannot track". |
| "Mandated by existence" | **Held if** | asserted | Held only by the job "the organism persists" — the very thing in question. |
| Average energy + entropy | **Borrowed** | thermodynamics | Renaming. The paper says informational ≠ thermodynamic free energy. |
| −½ ln 2πζ* | **Idle** | — | Constant in µ; drops out of the perception gradient. (Held for the variance job; tried in groups with the ½ ln σ terms.) |

## 4. Whole-explanation checks

**Flip.** An organism that dispersed — a fish out of water — is exactly what the theory says will not persist. The coarse flip passes. But p(ϕ) is the agent's *own* model (the note "formally p(ϕ) should be p(ϕ|m)"), so any behaviour can be made "expected" by crediting the agent with the right model. That is a patch made in advance. Its gauge, in Section 7, is the precision-weighted error on the agent's desired temperature: measurable, and it would show if the model were swallowing the job.

**Direction.** Poke the cause (μ̄, desired temperature) and the action moves. Poke the effect (warm the room) and μ̄ does not move. So it is not running backwards for action. For perception it *does* run from data to causes — legitimate for "what can we tell", and the paper keeps the two apart.

**Answer in the starting points.** "Organisms must minimise surprisal" sits very close to "organisms stay alive". If *viability* is doing the work, the conclusion is in the premise. What stops it being empty: it commits to a mechanism (variational inference on a brain-encoded model) that could be caught out. The "must" is asserted; the machinery is built.

**Jobs.** Every job is the owners'. My "covers a novel environment" and "splits action from perception correctly" are **added**, and held only if real.

**Pairs that pull.** (a) Precision sets the trade-off between moving µ and moving ϕ; the same error term is absorbed by either, the paper calls them "formally symmetric", and never fixes the split. Strengthen action and perception gives way. (b) The peakedness assumption pulls against the theory's own wish to encode large uncertainties: make the belief uncertain and the Taylor expansion fails.

**Change list leaves out.** Strong correlations (dropped up front, honestly); non-stationary priors; where the brain/environment boundary lies — called "functional", so any redrawing is allowed, which is loose; whether real neurons encode sufficient statistics — never tested.

**Rivals.** Action-as-control is, as the paper concedes, the same explanation as standard control at this level. Reinforcement learning with explicit reward is separated only by whether preferred states are written into the prior, and the paper never runs the change that would tell them apart. Say so: at this question they are one.

## 5. What would make it harder to vary

1. **Fix the action/perception split** — name the rule deciding how one error term is shared between µ and ϕ, and a measurement that would show the split is wrong.
2. **Replace "Gaussian" with "peaked and smooth"**, and state what breaks when noise grows. That turns a loose part into a held one and exposes the approximation's range.

## 6. What this does not show

Passing is not truth. The paper evaluates one implementation's assumptions; it explicitly does not settle the claims made for the brain.

## 7. One next step

Take the Section 7 agent, hold the reading fixed, and vary one precision. Write down which of action and perception gives way *before* running, then run it.
